# pagebuilder

## `resolveAuthors(ids, registry)` (async)

Resolve author records for a list of ids.

`registry.get(id)` returns a promise for the record of an id and rejects when the id is unknown. Returns a promise for the records of `ids` in the same order; if any request fails, the promise rejects with that error. The requests are independent and the backend has plenty of capacity, so they should not wait for each other.

prompt: `resolveAuthors` in `src/pagebuilder.js` is slow against the real backend: requests are made one after the other even though they are independent. Resolve author records for a list of ids. Fix it so it behaves as described in the README (results and error behaviour unchanged).

## `enrichRows(ids, geocoder)` (async)

Look up every row in a rate-limited geocoding service.

`geocoder.get(id)` returns a promise for the record of an id and rejects when the id is unknown. Returns a promise for the records of `ids` in the same order; if any request fails, the promise rejects with that error. The backend throttles clients that have more than 5 requests in flight at once, so use up to 5 concurrent requests (at least 3 when there is enough work) but never more.

## `recordsForEvents(keys, backend)` (async)

Records for a stream of events that mention the same entities repeatedly.

`backend.get(key)` returns a promise for the record of a key (rejecting for unknown keys). `keys` contains many repeated keys. Returns the records for `keys` in order; each distinct key must be requested only once, and requests may overlap. If a request fails the promise rejects with that error.

## `labelsFor(ids, registry)` (async)

Labels for a list of asset ids.

`registry.get(id)` answers one id (rejecting for unknown ids) and `registry.getMany(ids)` answers a whole list in one round trip with a `Map` of the ids that exist. Returns the values of the known ids of `ids` in order, skipping unknown ids.
